observations: GPR traces were ingested under the G-AID GPR 1.0 contract.
Product reported in this run: GPR Kirchhoff time migration (user velocity).
assumptions: Antenna 400.0 MHz was documented on the contract.
Bandpass used 0.2–2.0 × AntennaMHz because fLowHz/fHighHz were not supplied.
uncertainty: Two-way time is not depth unless a user velocity is applied.
A user velocity is not a measured dielectric structure.
Dewow, time-zero, SEC gain, and band-pass change amplitudes and apparent structure.
A visually enhanced radargram does not have improved geological certainty.
Band-pass status is recorded in process QC.
recommendations: Do not pick utilities, voids, or archaeology from a radargram without field verification.
Do not treat migrated depth as ground truth.
not_established: Measured depth is not established without an independently verified velocity.

files.formula: G-AID GPR 1.0 documented dt_ns, dx_m, AntennaMHz; amplitude as recorded

gpr_process_qc.json.time_zero_method: First sample where the mean absolute amplitude of the (dewowed) stack is ≥ 0.05 × the stack peak. Not a picked ground wave.
gpr_process_qc.json.sec_formula: gain(t) = max(t, dt)^n * exp(α t)  (Jol 2009 SEC; default n=2, α=0)

bandpass.formula: Butterworth SOS band-pass, order 4 unless overridden; filtfilt

gpr_process_qc.json.formula: optional dewow + optional time-zero + optional SEC + optional Nyquist-safe Butterworth (Jol 2009)
limitations: Dewow, time-zero, SEC gain, and band-pass are processing choices. A visually enhanced radargram does not have improved geological certainty.
Utilities, voids, archaeology, water table, and rebar are not established.

gpr_migrate_qc.json.formula: 2-D Kirchhoff time migration, zero-offset, constant velocity (Yilmaz 2001). z = 0.5 v t with the user velocity. No topography, no 3-D, not a measured depth model.
limitations: Migrated depth uses the supplied velocity and is not ground truth.
Hyperbola collapse does not prove a pipe, void, or archaeological feature.
The operator passed a noise-free constant-velocity diffraction benchmark. Field data are not that case.

interpretation_limit: A radargram is an observation. Overlay and colour scale do not prove a buried object.
